original_question: Let M(c2)=MH((2,0,c2)) be the moduli scheme of rank-two H-stable sheaves on a surface X with Chern classes (2,0,c2). Are all singularities of M(c2) canonical?
target_in_paper: §1, Problem 1.4: “Are all singularities of M(c2) canonical or not?”, with notation M_H((2,0,c2))=M(c2)=M set in the opening of §1 and motivation supplied by Theorem 1.2 and Proposition 1.3.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the relevant moduli space notation M(c2)=M_H((2,0,c2)), keeps the rank-two and c1=0 setup, and asks the same core yes/no question about whether the singularities are canonical that appears officially in the paper as Problem 1.4.
missing_details: The paper’s standing ground field is the complex numbers: X is a complex projective smooth surface.
In the surrounding setup of §1, X is not an arbitrary surface; it is assumed that κ(X)=1 and X is minimal, hence an elliptic surface.
The polarization H is not arbitrary in the paper’s setup: for v=(2,0,c2), H is assumed to be v-suitable.
M(c2) denotes the coarse moduli scheme of rank-two H-stable sheaves; the paper is not asking about a stack or an unspecified moduli functor.
The stability notion is the H-stability used in the Gieseker moduli construction cited in the paper.
The question concerns every singular point E in M(c2), i.e. whether each local singularity (M(c2),E) is canonical.
The draft sounds as if the question were posed for arbitrary surfaces X, but in the paper it is asked only in the c1=0 elliptic-surface setting of §1.

Problem 1.4 itself does not add hypotheses such as X generic or c2≫0; those appear only in nearby results (especially Theorem 1.2 and Theorems 1.5–1.7), so the quantifier should not be silently changed to a large-c2 statement.

The nearby motivation is that, together with Proposition 1.3 and the discussion immediately after it, canonical singularities would allow one to identify the Kodaira dimension from the pluricanonical/K-dimension picture.
refined_question: Let X be a complex projective smooth minimal surface with κ(X)=1, let v=(2,0,c2) for a fixed integer c2, and let H be a v-suitable ample line bundle on X. Write M(c2)=M_H(v) for the coarse moduli scheme of rank-two H-stable sheaves E on X with c1(E)=0 and c2(E)=c2. Is every singular point E in M(c2) a canonical singularity of the moduli scheme M(c2)?
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at §1, Problem 1.4. In §1 the paper first fixes the c1=0 elliptic-surface setting, then introduces the notation M_H((2,0,c2))=M(c2), and after Theorem 1.2 plus Proposition 1.3 explains why canonical singularities are important for understanding κ(M(c2)). It then asks exactly whether all singularities of M(c2) are canonical. The draft therefore has the right mathematical target, but it omits the paper’s standing hypotheses and can be misread as a much broader question about arbitrary surfaces. The nearby Theorems 1.5, 1.6, and 1.7 show that the paper’s intent is sharply focused on this elliptic-surface situation and on the local-singularity problem behind the Kodaira-dimension computation.
